Proof of immune mechanism: the direct antiglobulin (Coombs) test is positive with IgG 2+ and complement C3d 5+. The peripheral film shows spherocytes — the characteristic result of splenic macrophages removing IgG/complement-coated red cell membrane (partial extravascular haemolysis) — together with reticulocytosis and a reactive neutrophilia, which is typical of an acute haemolytic crisis. An IgG-positive (with C3d) DAT plus spherocytes defines warm autoimmune haemolytic anaemia.
